title: Tea in Vietnam: A Short History
titleVi: Trà ở Việt Nam: một chút lịch sử
intro: Minh, hướng dẫn viên, kể ngắn về lịch sử trà ở Việt Nam trước buổi thử trà: cây chè hoang, Thái Nguyên, trà đá vỉa hè và trà sen.

transcript.t: Tea has been part of Vietnamese life for many centuries, but nobody knows the exact year it began.
Many researchers believe wild tea first grew in the mountains where southern China and the north of Southeast Asia meet, including northern Vietnam.
In provinces like Ha Giang and Yen Bai, you can still find old Shan Tuyet tea trees growing in the forest.
So the tea plant is really at home here.
Exactly. Later, people planted tea in many places. Today Thai Nguyen is the most famous province for green tea.
Tea also became a way to show respect. When a guest arrives, the host makes tea before anything else.
Is it only for special occasions?
Not at all. Look at the street corners in Hanoi. People sit on small plastic stools and drink cheap iced tea with friends.
That's the luxury side. Hanoi families have scented green tea with lotus flowers for generations, and it was often a gift for important guests.
It sounds like tea connects everyday life and tradition.
That's a nice way to put it. Next, let's taste three teas and compare them.

write.prompt: A tourist asks: "Why is tea important in Vietnam?" Answer in 3–4 sentences: one fact about history, one about tradition and one about everyday life.
write.model: Tea has been part of Vietnamese life for centuries, and some wild tea trees in the north are very old. It is also a way to show respect, because we make tea for guests first. And it is part of everyday life: on Hanoi streets, friends drink cheap iced tea together.
